display.title: Episode 197: The Three Sacks of Gold
display.summary_short: Program number 197: serving Hashem with joy, Shema and a Mishnah by heart from a yeshiva boy, and the fable of the lazy artist who brought a mirror to the king.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi marks 197 weeks of Tzivos Hashem on the Air, thanks listeners for their letters, and hopes to keep broadcasting until Moshiach comes, then from Eretz Yisroel. Rattling his own spoon and chainik in Studio 604, he explains that thousands of children marching together is a mitzvah of serving Hashem with joy, and leads the Hakochainik march. After a sponsor message, a nine-year-old yeshiva boy tells what his class is learning, leads the Shema, and recites a Mishnah from Yoma by heart. Story time illustrates 'Yagati u'matzasi, ta'amin', one of the Twelve Pesukim: a king gives three artists thirty days to paint the walls of a room, with three sacks of gold for the best work. The first works from the very next morning, the second starts a week late, and the third does not appear until the last day, when he hangs a large mirror that reflects the other two paintings. The king hangs a sack of gold beside each real painting and tells the third artist to collect the two he 'earned' from the mirror. Uncle Yossi closes with a reminder of the 'My Mezuzah' contest.
display.lesson: Only real effort earns real reward: work hard and Hashem will help you succeed, and never claim credit for someone else's work.
